Order 
With the consent of the parties, the appeals are heard finally.

These appeals are arising out of a common award dated 10.05.2018 passed by the Member, MACT,
District Barwani therefore, they are heard together and disposed off by common order.
2.

These appeals have been filed preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 10.05.2018 by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8428 2 MA-3938-2018 Member, MACT, District Barwani in MACC Nos.84/2016 (M.A.No.3939/2018) and 103/2016 (M.A.No.3941/2018), whereby the survivors of deceased Giridhari and Sunil have been awarded an amount of Rs.8,86,000/- and Rs.9,88,000/- respectively.

sentences.text: 3. Brief facts of the case are that on 21.06.2016 at about 8.15 PM deceased Giridhari and Sunil were going to their house in motorcycle, Giridhari was sitting as a pillion rider in the vehicle and when they reached near A.B. Road T-junction, at that time, truck bearing No.MP 09/HG/9842 came in opposite direction, driven rashly and negligently, and collided with the motorcycle due to which both of them sustained grievous injuries and succumbed on the spot.

Thereafter the Smt. Sunita Bai vs Smt. Sunita on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95832876/
1 appellants/claimants filed applications under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 before the claims tribunal for compensation.

sentences.text: Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the impugned award dated 10.05.2018 passed by the claims tribunal the present appeals have been filed.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants in both the appeals submitted that the income has been assessed only as Rs.6,000/-, whereas the salary certificates Ex.- P14 (Giridhari) and Ex.-P/11 which is proved by Labour Contractor - Ram Mehar Singh (A.W.3) that the deceased Giridhari was earning basic wages of Rs.6,838/- plus 12% in the head of P.F and total amount of Rs.7,658/-, which should have been taken as income for assessing just and proper compensation.

Consortium has also been given at Rs.40,000/- whereas all the survivors no.1 to 4 are entitled for consortium @ Rs.40,000/-
per head and the amount should have been awarded Rs.1,60,000/-.
Looking to the age of the deceased Giridhari at 26 years 40% amount should have been added in the head of future prospectus.
It is hence NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8428 3 MA-3938-2018 submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.

5. In M.A.No.3941/2018, learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the deceased Sunil was having some income as deceased Girdhari which has been exhibited as Ex.P/11 and proved by Labour Contractor-Ram Mehar Singh (A.W.3).
In this case also he prays for allowing consortium amount of Rs.2,00,000/- for 5 survivors whereas only Rs.40,000/- has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
It is hence submitted that the amount awarded to the appellants be enhanced appropriately.
In the head of Future prospectus 40% should have been added in this case also as the deceased was 26 years of age.
On these submissions prayed for allowing the appeal and enhancement of award amount appropriately.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer of the appellants/claimants on the ground that amount awarded on all the heads in all the appeals have been addressed properly hence no interference is warranted and prayed for dismissal of the appeals.
7.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

8. In both the appeals M.A.No.3938/2018 and M.A. No.3941/2018 deceased Giridhari and Sunil were having total income of Rs.7,658/- as proved by their respective salary slips Ex.- P/11 and P/14 respectively.

It has been proved by examining done by Labour Contractor Ram Mehar Singh (A.W.3)
therefore, learned claims tribunal has committed error in not taking into account the aforesaid amount i.e. Rs.7,658/- in both the appeals.
In appeal M.A. No.3938/2021, 4 survivors will be awarded Rs.1,60,000/- as consortium and 40% in the head of Future Prospectus.

Thus just and proper NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8428 4 MA-3938-2018 compensation comes as under:
9.

In M.A.No.3638/2018 the appellants are entitled for the following enhanced amount :-
Smt. Sunita Bai vs Smt. Sunita on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95832876/
2 Rs.16,40,330/-
 Dependency  (Rs.7658 + 40% (FP) x 12-1/4 x 17)
 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Consortium Rs.1,60,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

Thus just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.9,44,330 /-
(enhanced amount of Rs.18,30,330 - amount awarded by Tribunal of Rs.8,86,000/-).
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.9,44,330/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
Findings as to pay and recover shall remain intact.

10. In M.A.No.3941/2018 the appellant is entitled for the following enhanced amount :-
Rs.16,40,330/-
 Dependency  (Rs.7658 + 40% (FP) x 12-1/4 x 17)

Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Consortium Rs.2,00,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

Thus just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.8,82,330 /-
(enhanced amount of Rs.18,70,330 - amount awarded by Tribunal of Rs.9,88,000/-).

Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8428 5 MA-3938-2018 Rs.8,82,330/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the claims tribunal.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
Findings as to pay and recover shall remain intact.

11. Since both the appeals have been valued at Rs.8,50,000/- and court fees has accordingly been paid therefore, the remaining court fees is to be paid within a period of 30 days as per the prevailing slab from the date of filing of the appeal.
In case the appellants fails to pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days then beyond 30 days interest will not be payable till filing of the Court fees.
